subtitle: Preserving history with effective and expiry dating

code:
CREATE TABLE analytics.dim_customer (
    customer_key   NUMBER,   -- unique per VERSION
    customer_id    VARCHAR,  -- repeats across versions
    region         VARCHAR,
    effective_date DATE,
    expiry_date    DATE,
    is_current     BOOLEAN
);
caption: The natural key can repeat; the surrogate key identifies one version, not one customer.

steps.label: Close old + insert new
steps.sub: MERGE has no clause for this

code:
UPDATE analytics.dim_customer AS tgt
SET expiry_date = CURRENT_DATE(), is_current = FALSE
FROM staging.customers_cleaned AS src
WHERE tgt.customer_id = src.customer_id
  AND tgt.is_current = TRUE
  AND tgt.region <> src.region;
caption: Must run first — step 2's anti-join depends on is_current already being updated.

code:
INSERT INTO analytics.dim_customer (customer_key, customer_id,
    region, effective_date, expiry_date, is_current)
SELECT HASH(src.customer_id, CURRENT_DATE()), src.customer_id,
    src.region, CURRENT_DATE(), NULL, TRUE
FROM staging.customers_cleaned AS src
LEFT JOIN analytics.dim_customer AS tgt
    ON tgt.customer_id = src.customer_id AND tgt.is_current = TRUE
WHERE tgt.customer_id IS NULL OR tgt.region <> src.region;
caption: One new current row per brand-new or just-closed-out customer.
